name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: Scaling is a clean 3.5x from the 4-serving source: chicken 1.35 lb -> 4 3/4 lb, corn 2 cups -> 7 cups, rice 1 cup -> 3 1/2 cups, jalapeno 1 -> 3 1/2. Consistent across every line.

All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step; no orphans, and no step introduces an unbought item. Two-amount buy strings map cleanly: Sea Salt (spice blend + rice), Cotija (salad + topping), Lime Juice/Lime Zest/Fresh Cilantro (rice + salad + topping).
The corn-salad quarter-teaspoon salt maps to the separate 'Salt' line (1 scant tsp scaled); the spice-blend and rice salt map to the 'Sea Salt' line. Kept prose generic ('salt', 'sea salt') to match.
Avocado browns in the fridge; portion_html instructs the reader to cube it day-of rather than at prep, and all fresh toppings are held to serving time.
Jalapeno and its heat are optional in the source; kept optional in the salad step.

No cost_lines were provided to me, so shop_smart makes only qualitative form/substitution claims (no per-ounce or 'lasts N batches' promises) that require no cost-line tracing. Only ${{cost_ps}}, {{cal}}, {{protein}} tokens used for figures; computed no numbers.
Macro self-check for the auditor: 44.6*4 + 53.8*4 + 21.5*9 = 587.1 kcal vs label 597, consistent within rounding/fiber.
Source title is singular 'Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl'; slug is plural. Cosmetic only, no action needed.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn is one of those things people line up for at a summer fair and then forget they can make at home for a fraction of the price. This bowl takes that same smoky, tangy, lime-soaked corn and builds a whole dinner around it. Seasoned chicken breast for the protein, cilantro lime rice for the base, and a creamy street corn salad that does the heavy lifting on flavor.

Here is the part that matters for your wallet and your week. One batch fills 14 containers, each one landing at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a real dinner, not a sad desk lunch, and it costs less than the drive-through you were about to settle for.
prose.shop_smart:
Chicken breast is the anchor, so buy it the way that makes sense: a large family pack rather than a little tray, then trim and cube it into one-inch chunks yourself. You handle the knife work, you keep the savings.

The original recipe used canned corn, drained, and that is exactly what I would reach for. It is already cooked, it drains in seconds, and it folds straight into the salad with no roasting or grilling to babysit. Fresh corn cut off the cob works if it is in season, but canned keeps this simple.

Greek yogurt carries the creamy tang that mayo usually owns, and it brings protein along for the ride instead of just fat. Look for cotija near the specialty cheese; if your store does not stock it, queso fresco or feta crumbles the same way and nobody will file a complaint. Round out the cart with limes, a bunch of cilantro, a jalapeno and a few avocados. Pick the limes firm and heavy, and choose avocados that are a day or two from ripe so they are ready when you build the bowls.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice, because it sets the pace. Bring the water to a boil, stir in the rice and sea salt, then cover it, drop the heat to low, and let it simmer about 20 minutes until tender. When it is done, toss the warm rice with chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice and lime zest so every grain picks up that bright cilantro lime flavor.

While the rice goes, build the street corn salad. In a big bowl combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, crumbled cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, chopped cilantro and salt. Stir it gently until it comes together, taste it, and adjust the seasoning. Set it aside to let the flavors get acquainted.

Now the chicken. Stir the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and sea salt together, then toss the cubed chicken until every piece is coated. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium, and once it is hot, lay the chicken in and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and reaches 165 degrees inside. Work in batches if your skillet is crowded, because a crowded pan steams instead of sears.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers, and the trick is to portion by weight, not by eyeball. Once the rice is done, spoon it across all 14 containers and even it out so each one carries the same base. Do the same with the chicken, dividing the cooked chunks evenly so nobody opens a container that is all rice and no protein.

The street corn salad goes on next, a generous scoop per container, spread over the chicken and rice. That is the part that makes each bowl taste like the fair.

Save the fresh toppings for the day you eat. Cubed avocado, sliced red onion, an extra crumble of cotija, a few cilantro leaves and a squeeze of lime go on right before it hits the table. Avocado browns in the fridge, so cut it fresh each morning rather than up front. Every container lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, which is why this one keeps you full to the next meal.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the math that matters. Fourteen dinners out of one afternoon, each one at about ${{cost_ps}} a serving, all in. That is street corn chicken bowls for less than a single fast-food combo, and you made 14 of them.

Cooking once and eating all week is the cheat code. You buy in bulk, you cook in bulk, and your cost per plate drops through the floor while the protein stays high. That is how you eat well without watching your grocery bill eat you.

head.description: Meal prep street corn chicken rice bowls: smoky seasoned chicken, cilantro lime rice, and a creamy Mexican street corn salad. High protein, budget friendly, makes 14 servings.
steps: Cook the rice: Bring the water to a boil, add the rice and sea salt, cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer about 20 minutes until tender. Toss the warm rice with chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice and lime zest.

Make the street corn salad: Combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, crumbled cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, diced jalapeno if using, chopped cilantro and salt. Stir gently, taste, and adjust the seasoning. Set aside.
Season the chicken: Stir together the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and sea salt, then toss the cubed chicken until every piece is fully coated.

Sear the chicken: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the chicken and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through and it reaches 165 degrees F, working in batches if the pan is crowded.
Portion the base: Divide the cilantro lime rice evenly among 14 containers, then divide the cooked chicken evenly over the rice.

Top the bowls: Add a generous scoop of the street corn salad to each container. Just before eating, add cubed avocado, sliced red onion, an extra crumble of cotija, cilantro leaves and a squeeze of fresh lime.
